clinician.final_diagnosis: Parainfectious optic neuritis following COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old previously healthy woman with confirmed COVID-19 infection (RT-PCR positive) presented with acute-onset vision loss and inferior altitudinal scotoma in the right eye. The patient had experienced a viral prodrome (fever, sore throat, fatigue) approximately 10 days prior to presentation, following COVID-19 exposure 15 days earlier. At initial presentation, ophthalmologic examination revealed reduced visual acuity (20/25 OD), relative afferent pupillary defect in the right eye, normal color vision with increased latency, and inferior altitudinal visual field defect on Humphrey Field Analyzer. Fundoscopic examination showed optic disc margin blurring with vessel tortuosity and dilatation, consistent with optic disc edema. Neuroimaging (gadolinium-enhanced MRI brain and spine) was normal, excluding demyelinating disease. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days, with documented resolution of disc edema in the inferior margin, and was discharged on oral prednisolone. At 3 weeks post-discharge, the patient reported subjective resolution of the inferior scotoma. The temporal relationship between viral infection/symptom resolution and subsequent optic neuritis onset, combined with the clinical and imaging findings, supports the diagnosis of parainfectious optic neuritis following COVID-19 infection.
